synthesis.evidence_balance: mixed — a clean balance sheet and reversible price-gap mechanics offset an ~97% FY26 EBITDA collapse, cash burn, and weakening trial.

bull_points.claim: The de-rate is a documented earnings/guidance shock, not a leverage or solvency event: gap-downs trace to the 2026-02-26 and 2026-05-07 earnings prints (with a founder departure and a butter wind-down), while the balance sheet stays net-debt/EBITDA 0.0x with interest coverage 99.4x.
bull_points.source_ref: EDGAR 8-K item codes at the gap-down dates (not blanket-labelled earnings)

bull_points.claim: Absolute revenue and EBITDA still grew over the full arc (revenue 74→784 and EBITDA -1→103 over FY17→FY25, LTM EBITDA $79M), so the collapsed trailing multiple sits on a base that had been rising, not a business already in absolute decline.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement (margin % + absolute EBITDA reconciler)

bull_points.claim: The load-bearing mechanism behind the reset is price-gap-driven, and management shows it is reversible: reducing the price gap at a top-10 customer from ~35% to ~25% lifted volumes 18% in two weeks vs the prior four.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Vital Farms, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Distribution momentum is expanding into the reset: an at-least-50% TDP increase secured with a top-3 customer and category-captain assignment, supporting a return to volume growth.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Vital Farms, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Quarterly average PDPs stepped up to 149.8 in Q1-26 from 144.8 in Q4-25 and 115.8 in Q1-25, with a guided 170–175 exit rate — a shelf-space leading indicator moving the right way through the shock.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Vital Farms, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: The name grows faster and carries far less leverage than the peer median (rev growth 26% vs 4%, Debt/EBITDA 0.1 vs 3.8) — inputs the human must weigh in judging whether the discount to peers is earned or residual, given the peer set is heterogeneous.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Operating Statistics (name vs peer median: growth/margin/leverage/beta)

bull_points.claim: Consensus target ($12 mean/median) sits near the current $13.82 price and one broker raised its target to $13 on 2026-06-30, so the sell-side no longer prices large further downside despite the negative FY26 marks.

bear_points.claim: Forward earnings power has collapsed, not just the trailing optic: FY26E EBITDA was cut from $123M to $3.4M (net -97%) and FY26 EPS crossed from +$1.54 to -$0.42 over the revision window — the real signal is a genuine forward earnings hole, not a stale trailing multiple.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (current-FY consensus path; ragged, absent lookbacks n/a)

bear_points.claim: The 1.2x EV/EBITDA vs peer 7.2x is optically cheap but the paired forward basis exposes it as a MISREAD of the trailing figure: NTM TEV/EBITDA is 70.81x (name) vs 8.98x peers, because FY26 EBITDA has been guided to near zero — the trailing multiple is cheap only against a collapsing denominator.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Trading Multiples (name row + Summary Statistics Low/Median/Mean/High)

bear_points.claim: The margin % fall is a real signal, not just an optical dip: EBITDA margin fell to a guided FY26 ~0% and absolute FY26E EBITDA fell to $3.4M from FY25 $103M — here the absolute figure confirms the % decline rather than reconciling it away.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement (margin % + absolute EBITDA reconciler)

bear_points.claim: The company is burning cash through the reset: LTM levered FCF is -$53.9M and FCF turned negative even as capex ran to -$100M, so the pristine 0.0x net-debt masks a self-funding gap.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Cash Flow 'Levered Free Cash Flow' [LTM 12 months Mar-29-2026]

bear_points.claim: The demand engine itself weakened: new-household share of consumers dropped to 50% in Q1-26 from more than 55% in 2024-2025, the direct evidence that price gaps choked new-customer acquisition.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Vital Farms, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

bear_points.claim: Revisions are uniformly negative and fresh: FY26 revenue breadth 0↑/3↓ and EPS 0↑/1↓ last month, with multiple brokers cutting FY26 revenue, EBITDA and ratings to Hold on 2026-05-08.

The pass-through cost structure amplifies the downturn: the company buys eggs from farmers regardless of the retail sales environment, so a demand shortfall creates a costly supply overhang that lands in margins.

decisive_question.question: Is the FY26 earnings collapse a one-year 'low watermark' reset from a reversible price-gap shock (overshoot), or the start of a structural erosion of Vital Farms' premium pricing power (value trap)?

evidence_for.claim: Narrowing the price gap at a top-10 customer from ~35% to ~25% lifted volumes 18% in two weeks — direct evidence the velocity loss is price-gap-driven and reversible.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Vital Farms, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

evidence_for.claim: Distribution is expanding through the reset (≥50% TDP increase with a top-3 customer; PDPs 149.8 vs 115.8 a year earlier), supporting a volume-led recovery path.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Vital Farms, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

evidence_for.claim: The balance sheet can absorb a reset year: net-debt/EBITDA 0.0x and interest coverage 99.4x leave room to fund the transition.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ Net Debt $3M [Q1 Mar-29-2026] ÷ CIQ EBITDA $80M [LTM 12 months Mar-29-2026]

evidence_against.claim: New-household trial fell to 50% from more than 55% — the growth engine (brand-awareness → trial conversion) weakened at these price gaps, suggesting the premium may be structurally capped.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Vital Farms, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

evidence_against.claim: FY26E EBITDA was slashed ~97% to $3.4M and FY26 EPS crossed to a loss, and the cash burn (LTM FCF -$53.9M) means the reset year consumes capital, not just optics.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (current-FY consensus path; ragged, absent lookbacks n/a)

evidence_against.claim: The pass-through egg-buying structure means demand shortfalls mechanically create a costly supply overhang, so margin damage is not purely a pricing choice management can fully reverse.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Vital Farms, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf

key_unknowns: Cash runway is not derived from the supplied facts — self-funding is flagged MIXED (latest-Q OCF < 0 and LTM FCF < 0); with capex ~$100M and no forward FCF guide, the burn duration is an unresolved BEARISH gap.

No forward/adjusted EV/EBITDA basis and no adjusted EPS in the revised guidance — the trailing 1.2x cannot be reconciled to a forward number, leaving overshoot-vs-terminal formally unresolved (EV/EBITDA note).
Single-segment (Eggs and Butter) reporting means no segment EBITDA breakout; the butter wind-down charge magnitude and its FY26 P&L drag are not quantified in the supplied facts — an opacity risk.
Covenant terms are UNKNOWN (extraction failed) and the JPMorgan revolver is shown undrawn but with no disclosed terms — liquidity headroom under a prolonged burn is not verifiable.
Whether FY26 is truly the 'low watermark' with FY27 recovery (consensus FY27E EBITDA $45.7M) depends on cost-structure actions whose 2027 impact management says is still to be realized — unconfirmed.

The 2026-08-06 next print is the checkpoint that would confirm or refute the committed $775–800M revenue / $0–$10M EBITDA outlook and the Q3 return to positive shell-egg volume growth — not yet resolved.
Peer set is HETEROGENEOUS (caps $50M–$78.0B, 1567x); whether the discount to the 7.2x peer median is earned or residual cannot be read cleanly off any single peer multiple.

caveats: EV/EBITDA cross-sheet gap — CIQ's Financials→Multiples reads 1.5x and its Comparable-Analysis sheet reads 1.2x on the same concept; verify which the verdict should use (a stale Close, a different pricing date, or an EBITDA basis) before reading either.
